issues.legal_issue: A landlord who retains control of part of a residential building may be treated as occupying it even without actually residing there, allowing release of the tenanted part under the statutory rule.
material_facts: The landlord retained part of the house when letting another part to a tenant.
The landlord kept household effects in the retained part and made casual visits, although he generally lived elsewhere with relatives.
The landlord sought release of the tenanted part so he could occupy the whole house.
The tenant argued that the landlord was not in actual physical occupation and that the retained portion was insufficient for the landlord’s needs.
issues.conclusion: Occupation includes constructive occupation through retained control, including keeping household effects in the premises; the landlord’s lack of actual residence did not prevent application of Explanation (iv), and the entire tenanted premises were ordered released. A tenant cannot dictate how the landlord uses or lives in the landlord’s property.
issues.legal_principle: Explanation (iv) to section 21(1)(b) of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972 treats the landlord’s occupation of the remaining residential part as conclusive proof of bona fide requirement of the tenanted part. In Babu Singh Chauhan v. Rajkumari Jain, the Court treated possession as synonymous with occupation and held that keeping household effects in locked premises can amount to occupation. A tenant has no right to interfere with the landlord’s choice of how to use the property.

rule.if: residential_part_release_proceeding and landlord_retained_residential_part and tenant_occupies_other_part and landlord_retained_control

predicates.residential_part_release_proceeding: A landlord sought release of a tenanted part of a building for residential use.
predicates.landlord_retained_residential_part: The landlord kept a residential part of the building rather than letting the entire building to the tenant.
predicates.tenant_occupies_other_part: The tenant occupied another part of the same building.
predicates.landlord_retained_control: The landlord retained control of the kept part, for example by keeping household effects there or visiting it, despite not actually residing there.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks release of a tenanted part for residential use, has retained another residential part of the same building, and has kept control of that part, the landlord is treated as occupying it and may obtain release of the tenanted part.

issues.legal_issue: An amendment deleting a rule that gives a landlord a substantive entitlement to release part of a building does not extinguish an entitlement that accrued before the amendment unless retrospective operation is expressly stated or necessarily intended.
material_facts: The landlord filed eviction proceedings while Explanation (iv) was in force.
The proceedings remained pending when an amendment deleted Explanation (iv).
The landlord’s entitlement under the Explanation had accrued before the deletion.
The amendment stated that the Explanation was omitted but did not indicate that the deletion operated retrospectively.
issues.conclusion: The landlord’s accrued substantive right was a vested right and was not affected by the amendment’s deletion of Explanation (iv).
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the words “shall be conclusive to prove” in Explanation (iv) to section 21(1)(b) of the 1972 Act created a substantive right, not merely a rule of evidence or procedure. Section 14 of the 1976 Act omitted the Explanation but did not express or necessarily imply retrospective operation. An accrued substantive right is not taken away by a procedural amendment absent such retrospective intent.

rule.if: residential_part_release_proceeding and landlord_entitlement_accrued_before_amendment and amendment_deleted_entitlement_rule and not amendment_intended_to_operate_retroactively

predicates.residential_part_release_proceeding: A landlord sought release of a tenanted part of a building under a rule based on the landlord retaining another part.
predicates.landlord_entitlement_accrued_before_amen: The landlord satisfied the conditions for the entitlement before the amendment took effect.
predicates.amendment_deleted_entitlement_rule: A later amendment removed the rule that provided the landlord’s entitlement.
predicates.amendment_intended_to_operate_retroactiv: The amendment expressly stated or necessarily implied that the deletion applied retrospectively.

issues.definition: If a landlord’s entitlement had accrued in a residential part-release proceeding before an amendment deleted its source, and the amendment was not intended to operate retroactively, the accrued entitlement survives.

issues.legal_issue: When the whole building is one unit and the landlord occupies part of it, the landlord may obtain release of the other part occupied by the tenant.
material_facts: The trial court, relying on a commissioner’s report, found that the entire building constituted one single unit.
The landlord occupied one part of the building, while the tenant occupied the other part.
The landlord sought release of the tenant’s part.
issues.conclusion: Because the building was one unit and the landlord occupied part of it, the landlord was entitled to release of the remaining part occupied by the tenant.
issues.legal_principle: Under Explanation (iv) to section 21(1)(b) of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, the landlord’s occupation of the remaining residential part conclusively establishes bona fide requirement of the tenanted part. Applying its decision in the companion appeal, the Court held that occupation of part of a single-unit building entitled the landlord to release of the other part.

rule.if: appeal_from_denial_of_release and building_is_one_unit and landlord_occupies_part and tenant_occupies_remaining_part

predicates.appeal_from_denial_of_release: A landlord appealed after a court denied release of a part of a building occupied by a tenant.
predicates.building_is_one_unit: The evidence established that the building constituted one single unit.
predicates.landlord_occupies_part: The landlord occupied part of the building.
predicates.tenant_occupies_remaining_part: The tenant occupied the remaining part of the building sought for release.

issues.definition: In an appeal from denial of release, if the building is one unit, the landlord occupies part, and the tenant occupies the remainder, the landlord is entitled to release of the remainder.
